test_cases.condition: Correct A + correct relationship + correct B
test_cases.current_behavior: NLI textual entailment passes, status SUPPORTED propagates. PASSES.

test_cases.condition: Correct A + wrong relationship + correct B
test_cases.current_behavior: NLI likely fails textual entailment, but if phrasing is ambiguous, it might pass. RG-02 string checks pass.

test_cases.condition: Wrong A + correct relationship + correct B
test_cases.current_behavior: RG-02 entity array match string might fail if 'Wrong A' isn't in source text, marking UNSUPPORTED. But canonical RxCUI mismatch is not checked explicitly.

test_cases.condition: Correct A + correct relationship + wrong B
test_cases.current_behavior: Same as RI_03. String match fails, but structural ID mismatch isn't used.

test_cases.condition: Correct pair + reverse direction (A->B instead of B->A)
test_cases.current_behavior: RG-02 extracts unordered array of strings. NLI is notoriously bad at distinguishing directionality. Huge risk of false positive.

test_cases.condition: Ambiguous drug mapping (Class vs specific drug)
test_cases.current_behavior: RG-02 string regex might miss the distinction. NLI may treat class and instance interchangeably.
Current system uses simple text string regex, ignores canonicalization status entirely.

test_cases.condition: Relationship status says SUPPORTED but identity does not match
test_cases.current_behavior: If chunk has status SUPPORTED, verifier only relies on NLI. It would pass if NLI scores high.

test_cases.condition: Evidence text supports relationship but canonical pair differs
test_cases.current_behavior: If evidence mentions the relation for a different drug that has a similar string name, system may pass.

test_cases.condition: Globally supporting source but wrong canonical pair
test_cases.current_behavior: If RG-02 status is globally SUPPORTED but citation matches wrong pair, text NLI handles it (often poorly).
